name: Bulk Carrier Pre-Management Takeover Inspection
notes: Exact source template data. Blank observation cells are intentionally absent. Formula strings are reference material, not observed results. Quantities are template recommendations until confirmed against vessel-specific requirements.

headers.D: Detailed inspection / test to be carried out

cells.D: Verify vessel name, IMO, flag, port of registry, class, owner, DOC company, technical manager, crew manager, P&I, H&M and trading area. Cross-check all against certificates and class status.
cells.E: All identities consistent; no unresolved ownership/manager discrepancy.

cells.D: Obtain current class status report directly from vessel/office. Review class notation, survey status, Conditions of Class, Recommendations, Memoranda, overdue items, damage surveys and outstanding statutory recommendations.
cells.E: No overdue class/statutory item affecting safe trading. Any open item has agreed rectification plan, budget and class acceptance.

cells.D: Check issue/expiry/endorsement dates and survey windows for all statutory certificates; compare originals onboard with office matrix.
cells.E: No expired certificate; no survey overdue; upcoming 180/90/60/30-day items identified.

cells.D: Review last 36 months PSC, flag, class and RightShip/RISQ reports. Identify repeat deficiencies, detentions, ISM-related findings and unresolved CAPA.
cells.E: All findings closed with objective evidence; repeat deficiencies specifically risk-assessed.
cells.F: PSC Form A/B, flag/class reports, RISQ

cells.D: Review last internal audit, SMC audit, DOC-related vessel findings, NCs and corrective actions. Interview Master/CE on open findings.
cells.E: No overdue NC/CAPA; evidence supports closure; crew familiar with current SMS.

cells.D: Open live PMS with Chief Engineer. Export overdue jobs by department, critical equipment jobs, postponed jobs and jobs overdue >30/>90 days. Sample-check completion evidence against engine/deck logs.
cells.E: Critical PMS overdue = 0. Any non-critical backlog quantified and takeover rectification plan agreed.

cells.D: Verify SMS/PMS list of critical equipment and operational tests. Confirm redundancy arrangements and last test dates.
cells.E: Company-approved critical equipment list exists; critical failures/degraded redundancy explicitly recorded.
cells.F: SMS critical equipment list, test logs

cells.D: Review deck, engine, electrical, cargo gear and safety defect lists. Reconcile with PMS, class status, requisitions and superintendent reports.
cells.E: One consolidated defect register. No unrecorded safety-critical defect.

cells.D: Review all open requisitions/POs, especially safety-critical and machinery spares. Confirm delivery location/status and budget commitment.
cells.E: No safety-critical requisition stalled without approved action or substitute.

cells.D: Review last 24 months overhaul reports, performance reports, indicator cards, liner/piston/exhaust valve records, turbocharger service, crankcase inspections and alarm history.
cells.E: History traceable; next major maintenance and remaining running hours known.

cells.D: Review running hours, major overhaul dates, load test/performance, black-start readiness, repeated alarms and lube oil trends.
cells.E: At least required generating redundancy is dependable; no unresolved repeated load-sharing problem.

cells.C: Lube oil / fuel / cooling water analysis
cells.D: Review trend reports, abnormal alerts and closure actions for ME, AE, gear/shaft, hydraulics, boiler/cooling water and fuel quality.
cells.E: No uninvestigated abnormal trend; latest samples within company/maker interval.

cells.D: Review last docking specification, completion report, underwater repairs, propeller/rudder/shaft measurements, sea valves, thickness measurements and next docking due.
cells.E: Major repair history understood; no deferred docking work creating takeover risk.

cells.D: Review at least previous 24–36 months breakdowns, off-hire, towage, grounding/contact, major repairs and insurance claims. Reconcile with logbooks and service records.
cells.E: All material events declared and technically closed; residual risks identified.

cells.D: Compare 12-month consumption and speed records with charter/owner figures. Identify deterioration, abnormal cylinder oil, AE fuel, freshwater or electrical load.
cells.E: Baseline established for takeover; abnormal consumption investigated.
cells.F: Noon reports, bunker records, performance reports

cells.D: Explain inspection scope. Ask Master and CE separately for their top five technical/safety concerns, recurring defects, spare shortages and expected major jobs next 6 months.
cells.E: Concerns recorded verbatim and cross-checked during inspection.

cells.D: Interview OOW, 2/E, 3/E, bosun and key ratings on emergency duties, critical equipment, enclosed space, hot work, steering emergency operation, OWS and cargo hold water ingress alarms.
cells.E: Key personnel demonstrate practical familiarity; gaps entered as takeover training actions.

cells.D: Inspect visible shell, bow/stern, draft marks, load line, damage, buckling, wastage, temporary repairs and sea-chest/discharge areas where visible.
cells.E: No significant deformation, uncontrolled corrosion or temporary repair affecting seaworthiness.

cells.D: Walk full weather deck. Inspect corrosion, grooving, cracks, wasted doublers, welded repairs, deck penetrations and coating breakdown.
cells.E: No structural defect requiring class notification; suspect areas measured/referred.

cells.D: Inspect heads, floats, flame screens where fitted, gaskets, closing devices, caps and corrosion at deck penetration.
cells.E: All closing devices functional; no holed/wasted heads; markings legible.

cells.D: Inspect and operate representative doors, manholes, skylights, store doors and engine casing closures; check gaskets, dogs and remote indications.
cells.E: All required closures close effectively and are not seized or defeated.

cells.D: Enter only gas-freed tanks under permit. Select representative forward/midship/aft tanks if possible. Inspect coating, corrosion, frames, brackets, ladders, piping, anodes and mud accumulation.
cells.E: No serious structural defect; coating condition and corrosion risk graded; inaccessible tanks supported by latest internal inspection photos/report.

cells.D: Inspect accessible spaces for corrosion, leakage, coating, piping and cleanliness.
cells.E: No active leakage or serious wastage; access arrangements safe.

cells.D: Inspect each accessible hold: side frames, lower/upper brackets, hopper/topside areas, tank top, bulkheads, stool areas and previous repairs. Note cracks, buckling, indentations and heavy corrosion.
cells.E: No visible structural damage requiring immediate class attendance; all suspect areas photographed and located.

cells.D: Assess hold cleanliness, coating breakdown, rust scale, cargo residues, contamination and suitability for anticipated trades.
cells.E: Condition documented; any major coating/rust scale work estimated.

cells.D: Open and inspect bilge wells, strainers, suction, non-return valves and remote alarms. Test suction where practical.
cells.E: Bilges clean and operational; non-return protection effective; high-level alarms function.

cells.D: Test all cargo hold and forward-space water ingress alarms from sensors and panel. Verify fault monitoring and alarm records.
cells.E: All required channels operational with no bypass/fault.

cells.D: Inspect each panel for distortion, cracks, wasted plating, hydraulic leaks, hinges, wheels, chains and operating mechanism.
cells.E: Panels structurally sound and operate smoothly without unsafe manual intervention.

cells.D: Inspect rubber for permanent set, hardening, cuts, compression and joints. Check spare rubber/profile onboard.
cells.E: Continuous effective packing; no significant hardening/damage; spare stock available.

cells.D: Inspect for corrosion, grooving, deformation and previous weld repairs. Check landing pads and supports.
cells.E: Bars smooth and intact; no major wastage affecting sealing.

cells.D: Inspect representative cleats and all visibly defective items. Verify adjustment, rubber washers and securing.
cells.E: All hatch securing devices complete, correctly adjusted and operable.

cells.D: Clean/test hatch drain channels and non-return arrangements; verify drainage paths not blocked.
cells.E: Free drainage; non-return function satisfactory.

cells.D: Review latest ultrasonic/hose/chalk test; conduct spot test if permitted, especially suspect panels.
cells.E: Recent satisfactory tightness evidence and no signs of cargo wet damage.

cells.D: Inspect all cranes for corrosion, cracks, pedestal/foundation condition, jib structure, slewing ring area and access ladders/platforms.
cells.E: No structural crack/deformation; inspection points accessible and safe.

cells.D: Inspect full accessible length, end terminations, sheaves and drums. Review renewal date, lubrication and discard criteria.
cells.E: No broken-wire/corrosion/diameter-loss condition beyond maker/class criteria; renewal history known.

cells.D: Operationally test hoist/luff/slew brakes, limit switches, emergency stop and alarms where safe.
cells.E: All safety functions operate correctly.

cells.D: Check hydraulic pumps, motors, hoses, leaks, oil condition, filters, coolers and standby arrangements.
cells.E: No significant leak; pressures/temperatures normal; critical hoses/spares available.

cells.D: Verify register, annual thorough examination, 5-year load tests as applicable, certificates for hooks, blocks, shackles, spreaders and grabs.
cells.E: Certificates current and gear ID matches physical markings.

cells.D: Inspect shells, pins, sheaves, wires, hydraulic system, closing mechanism and certification.
cells.E: Serviceable with critical consumables/spares available.

cells.D: Operate where possible. Check foundation, guards, brakes, clutches, controls, hydraulic/electric leaks, emergency stops and warping ends.
cells.E: Safe operation; guards complete; no serious foundation or brake defect.

cells.D: Review brake holding/test records and inspect brake linings, drums, adjustment and markings.
cells.E: Records current; no oil contamination or excessive wear.

cells.D: Check certificates, line-management records, condition, chafing, retirement criteria, storage and spare lines.
cells.E: All working lines serviceable; minimum company spare reserve available.

cells.D: Inspect wear, corrosion, free movement, securing, foundations and sharp edges.
cells.E: No structural defect or seized roller creating line hazard.

cells.D: Inspect visible chain, bitter end arrangements, stoppers and windlass. Review latest calibration.
cells.E: Calibration within limits; no missing/stuck securing arrangements.

cells.D: Check both units where fitted, licenses, chart updates, sensors, alarms, backup arrangement and officer familiarization.
cells.E: Operational with current ENCs and backup arrangement; no unresolved alarm/fault.

cells.D: Test radars, performance monitor, guard zones, ARPA, inputs and controls.
cells.E: Both required radars operational.

cells.D: Compare repeaters, alarm status and service history.
cells.E: Accurate and all required repeaters functional.

cells.D: Check deviation card, illumination, condition and comparison error.
cells.E: Usable, current deviation information.

cells.D: Verify operation, alarm status, sensor inputs and self-tests.
cells.E: Required units operational.

cells.D: Verify operational status, static data, testing records and security procedure.
cells.E: Correct static data and required systems operational.

cells.D: Check annual performance test, alarms, recording status and recovery media.
cells.E: No active fault; APT current.

cells.D: Test modes, stages, resets and records of use.
cells.E: Functional and used in accordance with procedure.

cells.D: Test required equipment, batteries, reserve source, printers/logs and annual radio survey.
cells.E: All required GMDSS equipment operational; batteries within capacity/life.

cells.D: Test panel, failure alarms, spare lamps/LED modules, whistles and shapes.
cells.E: All required signals operational and spares available.

cells.D: Test bridge controls, NFU, changeover, rudder indicators and communication with steering gear room.
cells.E: Normal and emergency control arrangements proven.

cells.D: Review recent berth-to-berth plan, UKC, no-go areas, chart corrections, Master/Pilot exchange, standing/night orders.
cells.E: Recent voyage demonstrates SMS compliance and proper BRM practice.

cells.D: Test sample detectors across accommodation, engine room and stores; check panel faults/bypasses and zone plans.
cells.E: No unauthorized bypass/fault; alarms audible/visible.

cells.D: Run each main fire pump; record pressure and check remote/local starting where fitted.
cells.E: Required pumps deliver stable pressure without abnormal leakage/vibration.

cells.D: Start locally and from required arrangement; verify suction, priming and two-jet capability where practical.
cells.E: Immediate reliable start and adequate pressure.

cells.D: Inspect representative full route for leaks/corrosion; check hoses/nozzles and international shore connection.
cells.E: System ready for immediate use; no wasted/leaking section.

cells.D: Check service date, bottle weights/levels, release cabinet seals, alarms, time delay, instructions and space closure arrangements.
cells.E: Certification current; release arrangements secured and unobstructed.

cells.D: Operationally test selected fuel quick-closing valves and remote stops for fans, pumps and machinery in accordance with safe procedure.
cells.E: All tested items operate and reset correctly.

cells.D: Inspect and operate representative fire doors, dampers, skylights and ventilation flaps.
cells.E: Close effectively; no hooks/wedges defeating fire integrity.

cells.E: Statutory quantity complete; all units ready; spare charge arrangement compliant.

cells.E: Matches approved fire plan; no overdue unit.

cells.E: Ready for independent operation.

cells.E: Safety trips/protections functional; no dangerous leakage.
